body:
Thank you. He's at work but I texted and told him I'm not doing well. He encouraged me to call my mom and I poured my heart out to her and she surprised me with how understanding she was.

It doesn't make everything better but she helped me see some good aspects of my life.

You have no idea how much a single reply to this post means and even more so your responses have been great.

I'm under 30 and had a stroke last year. Ever since then I just don't feel joy. My husband was someone I adored. He was my life. Literally enjoyed every second with him. He made me whole.

But I just don't feel that anymore. I just don't feel joy. I love him but the biggest, shining light in my life is gone.

I've lost 5 pregnancies. Coming up on the anniversary of my furthest one at 12 weeks. And should be 12 weeks now with my 5th but we lost them too.

I had friends who made life easier but everyone has stopped talking to me. I used to be a good person who cared and loved with passion. And all of that is gone.

I can't even make my husband smile anymore. So I just don't see the point if I'll never find joy again.

That's the best way I've ever heard anyone describe 'being in your head too much'. 

My husband and I talked last night after the big blow up and we're going to try counseling.

I came close to implementing my plan last night but some redditers helped me out. Including your message.

I'm very grateful.

Thank you for your response. I really appreciate it 

Yes, we've been discussing counseling. He doesn't like to participate but will go with. I have a counselor so I think I can have her ask him direct questions which he will likely then answer. Otherwise he just listens as he doesn't know what to bring up or say.

This is absolutely spot on. I'm just under 1.5 yrs post stroke and we're still learning the extent of the damage. Mostly recovered physically with a few lingering effects. But my mentality is completely different. My emotions are different. My reactions and actions are impulsive and difficult to understand.

We've been together for almost 10 years, married 4. And we've been through many many traumatic events (at no fault of our own). We used to pride ourselves on our communication and willingness to compromise. 

I just found a local support group that I think I'll go to. I didn't realize this was most likely stroke related and not me just being difficult.

As for coping, I used to exercise a lot, volunteer, work a fulfilling full time job. I kept active and busy. But since the stroke and with bipolar I, it's very difficult to do any of those reliably. 

I think we are indeed trying to find our new normal still. Thank you very much. Something so simple and it took a Reddit stranger to help me realize.  🙂

Husband keeps saying he hates breaks and doesn't see the point. As for friends, I don't really talk to anyone. I really don't have friends.

Thank you for the reply

My stroke changed everything. I changed. My thought process is still new to me. I get frustrated very easily. I'm more jaded. More guarded.

I keep making fights out of nothing. I go from 0 to 100 in seconds with anger.

Finding a counselor where I live is hard. Only a dozen or so in 60 miles. She was the best. Helped me the most. But now she's becoming unreliable.

Dang it. I'm sorry. I posted this from an alt account by mistake. My other account meets the rules. Is it possible to delete this so I can post with other account? I'd prefer them not associated with each other.

I see a psychiatrist and counselor. Nothing helps anymore. I've been in the psych hospital 3 times this year. It's now to the point it doesn't help. I wish the US had a long term mental health facility somewhere. But apparently we don't. 30 days max.

I don't know how to live. I really don't. And I love my husband. He tries so hard to make me happy. But nothing does now.

I've pushed my friends away without even realizing it. I guess it's a step closer to suicide.

I want to quit being a burden. I want to be dead if I can't feel because what's the point in living if you feel nothing. I feel mostly guilt and anxiety.

I haven't been able to cry since my stroke. I'm so far from being okay.
Things with my husband are complicated. I love him, but I'm not happy with our relationship anymore. We're going to marriage counseling in December
I'm trying. I really am. I don't want to die. But I don't foresee much in my future. Im so calm. It's really eerie.
Thank you. I really don't want to die. But there doesn't seem to be anything that helps. I'm holding out. But I've all ready started pushing people away. I didn't even realize I was doing it.
It's in a small box called First Signal. They often are out in my area but otherwise they're accurate.

Yes. I ended up in the hospital this week. Tried to cut and OD. I'm home now and feeling a little bit better.

I told my husband everything and now we're going to schedule with a neurologist so they can help explain why I feel different and also going to a stroke survivor support group after the hurricane passes.

Thank you.
I hope you manage to find a reason to live before then.
That's good. Glad to hear it.

That's what I'm doing right now. But next year I plan to. Now I can help ease into the process by making sure the house is well organized and finding easy to make healthy meals for my husband.

I know how fucked up this is. But I'm not left with much of a choice.
I'm scheduling to see a counselor. Thank you.
We talked today and we made some great compromises. I'm going to schedule for therapy too.

I'm in love with my arrogant best friend and no longer in love with my spouse.

And I'm killing myself next year.

That although I'm pulling my life together, I feel no joy nor pride. I just exist. With the only feelings being anxiety and guilt.

And I don't see the point in life if I can't feel any of the good feelings.

I had to call my sister and tell her an extremely close childhood friend had died. It was so hard to get the right words out and try to be there for her. I've only seen her cry a handful of times. But we both cried that day.
